question.text: Per the chapter, why is the Mark-to-Market method preferred over Amortised Cost for valuing traded money market and debt securities in a Cat III AIF?

answer.text: MTM better reflects default-risk changes from credit downgrades, and is more transparent, reducing manager discretion
Amortised cost is prohibited by RBI
MTM is always at premium to amortised cost

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the chapter: 'Using the Mark-to-Market approach for valuation reduces the potential default risk inherent in a fixed income security, due to a downgrade in the credit rating of a specific security. Instead of using Amortized Cost approach of valuation, mark-to-market method is more reliable and transparent, although it may reduce the discretion of managers in the valuation process.' The workbook references FBIL/CCIL/FIMMDA and exchange prices as inputs for MTM of debt and money-market instruments. The Trap: MTM is not cheaper than amortised cost operationally; RBI does not prohibit amortised cost; MTM is not always at a premium to amortised cost. Note: The workbook's rationale rests on better reflection of credit-risk changes, greater transparency, and reduced manager discretion - not on cost or any blanket regulatory prohibition.
